package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in the report. The article discusses incident response and revocation strategies for compromised accounts and images in a Sigstore-enabled software supply chain, but does not analyze or present any particular malicious package or code.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual signing activity from a single identity (e.g., dev.a@example.com signing many images in a short period)
Signatures for images from accounts not normally authorized to deploy
Artifacts present in transparency log but not in build logs
file_indicators: Container images signed by compromised accounts
Image digests (sha256:...) associated with unauthorized signatures
network_indicators: Signatures posted to Sigstore transparency log (Rekor)
Unusual access to container registries or CI/CD systems
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Sigstore transparency logs for signatures issued by identities in your organization, especially for anomalous activity (e.g., unexpected images, high signing volume, or images not present in build logs). Cross-reference image digests in the transparency log with your deployment and build records. Blocklist image digests associated with compromise. Monitor for changes in allowed signers in admission controller policies.
